## Purpose and Entry Points
`playwright-cli` is a Node.js command-line interface for browser automation by coding agents. It wraps Playwright operations in concise commands and supplies agent-readable SKILL documentation. Primary executable entry point: `playwright-cli.js`; package publication/runtime metadata: `package.json`.

## CLI Command Boundary
The CLI accepts session-scoped commands for browser lifecycle, navigation, interaction, snapshots, storage, network routing, diagnostics, recording, and dashboard access. Commands act on a selected/default browser session and return page state or write artifacts rather than embedding full page data into agent context. Core command implementation boundary: `playwright-cli.js`; command-level integration coverage: `tests/integration.spec.ts`.

## Browser Session Lifecycle
A session owns a Playwright browser/context/page state, preserving cookies and storage across CLI invocations while it remains alive. Sessions may be isolated in memory, persistent on disk, or attached to an existing Chromium-family browser through CDP/extension mechanisms. Session management includes named sessions, listing, graceful close, forced process termination, detach, and data deletion. Relevant entry points: `playwright-cli.js`, `README.md`.

## Page Interaction and Snapshot Flow
An agent opens or navigates a page, receives or explicitly captures a snapshot, then targets elements using snapshot refs, CSS selectors, or Playwright locators. Interaction commands—typing, clicking, forms, keyboard/mouse actions, uploads, tabs, and dialogs—mutate the selected page. Snapshots and searches are the principal token-efficiency boundary: page structure is emitted as a file/reference-oriented representation rather than a full accessibility tree in command output. Relevant paths: `playwright-cli.js`, `skills/playwright-cli/SKILL.md`.

## State, Network, and Artifact Boundaries
The CLI exposes browser-state save/load plus cookie, localStorage, and sessionStorage operations. It also manages request routing/mocking and exposes console/request inspection. Screenshots, PDFs, snapshots, traces, and videos are material outputs; configuration controls output location and whether logs/artifacts go to files or stdout. Supporting agent guidance is separated into focused references: `skills/playwright-cli/references/storage-state.md`, `skills/playwright-cli/references/request-mocking.md`, `skills/playwright-cli/references/tracing.md`.

## Agent Skill Distribution
The repository ships a portable skill package that teaches agents how to invoke the CLI and complete specialized workflows such as test execution, code execution, test generation, video capture, and element inspection. Installation/update behavior is supported by repository scripts rather than a web service. Primary paths: `skills/playwright-cli/SKILL.md`, `scripts/update.js`, `skillCheck.js`.

## Runtime, Infrastructure, and Delivery
Runtime requirements are Node.js 18+ plus Playwright and installed/available browser engines. External browser connections can use Chrome DevTools Protocol or a browser extension; remote browser/service endpoints are configurable. CI and npm publication are automated through GitHub Actions. Relevant paths: `package.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/publish.yml`.
